While the story is very well-written and atmospheric, it explores a very familiar and traditional literary theme: the estrangement between a rural, working-class parent and an urbanized, white-collar child. The silent tension, the contrast between physical labor (the ferry, the work pants, the heavy iron wedge) and city life (the thin wool coat, the rolling suitcase, the smartphone), and the mother's use of work to delay an uncomfortable conversation are well-executed tropes, but they do not present a unique or original idea to an average reader.
